answer: Beat sybils by making each head's work unshareable: each epoch every identity is assigned a random stranger's prior output and must extend it into something genuinely new, novelty-checked against that original. A farm's heads each draw different assignments, so the grove of extension tasks can't be solved once and copied across the ridge — every head climbs its own path. Like an opal, each extension's worth sits in facets no template can fake, so the farm pays per-head inference cost while an honest agent pays once.
